# Reference

Everything the plugin does, beyond the [README](../README.md).

## The OpenCode version

Each release is built and tested against one OpenCode V2 version: the exact `@opencode/plugin`
version in its `package.json`. Every release and its version:

OpenCode never checks the version. The plugin loads on any host from 2.0.4 on, but its tools may
break on another version. The terminal part is tested on OpenCode 2.4.1 only. On a version other
than the pinned one, the plugin writes a warning to the server log when it loads
(`opencode serve --print-logs` shows it).

## Updating the plugin

OpenCode checks a plugin for updates only when its entry is not an exact version.
`opencode-courier`, `opencode-courier@latest` and `opencode-courier@^0.2.0` are checked;
`opencode-courier@0.2.1` never is. To fix an exact entry, replace it and restart OpenCode:

```bash
opencode plugin remove opencode-courier@0.2.1   # the entry as it appears in plugins
opencode plugin add opencode-courier
```

`opencode plugin check` then shows `(update available)` when there is one, and
`opencode plugin update` installs it. An `opencode-courier@latest` or range entry installs it on its
own, at a start and every 24 hours, also a release pinned to a newer OpenCode than yours; the bare
name waits for `opencode plugin update`. A failed check reads as "no update" and is only logged
(`failed to check plugin update` in `~/.local/share/opencode/log/`); look at your `.npmrc`'s
registry and proxy settings.

## Options

The server options go on the plugin's entry in the **global** config,
`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`. From a local clone, `package` is the path to its `dist`
directory.

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [{ "package": "opencode-courier", "options": { "maxDepth": 2 } }]
}
```

| Option | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `maxDepth` | `5` | The deepest a spawned session may be. Your session is depth 0. |
| `maxChildren` | `5` | Live children one session may have. |
| `maxTotal` | `30` | Live spawned sessions in one tree; the top is not counted. |

The limits are positive integers. A value that is not valid keeps the default, and the server log
says so. A change applies once OpenCode loads the plugin again. The `webhook`, `memory` and
`nativeChildren` options are not read; remove them from the config. A child is
[native](#native-child-sessions) only when its spawn passes `native: true`.

The terminal part gets no options from `opencode.json`. It reads them from its own config,
`~/.config/opencode/cli.json`:

```jsonc
// ~/.config/opencode/cli.json
{
  "plugins": [{ "package": "opencode-courier", "options": { "animations": false } }]
}
```

| Option | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `animations` | `true` | `false` keeps the [tree panel](#the-tree-panel) still: no spinner, flash or moving mole. |

Git is looked for in `/usr/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin` and
`/run/current-system/sw/bin` (on Windows, `C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe` and its `(x86)` twin),
never through `PATH`. Set `OPENCODE_COURIER_GIT` to an absolute path, in the server's environment,
for a git elsewhere.

## The tools

`?` marks an optional parameter.

| Tool | Parameters | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `courier_spawn` | `task`, `title?`, `agent?`, `model?`, `variant?`, `isolate?`, `native?` | Creates a session, sends it the task and a brief, and returns at once. `model` and `variant` choose [what it runs on](#the-model-a-child-runs-on). `isolate: true` gives it its own [worktree](#worktrees). `native` says whether it is an OpenCode subagent ([native child sessions](#native-child-sessions)). Refused past the [limits](#session-trees-and-their-limits). |
| `courier_send` | `sessionID`, `message`, `status?`, `artifacts?` | Delivers a message, waking the session if idle. A running turn reads it at its next step, after the tool call in progress returns, and nothing is cut short. From a child to its parent, a `status` makes it the child's [report](#a-childs-report). |
| `courier_tree` | `sessionID?` | One look at the [whole tree](#seeing-and-stopping-a-subtree) under this session (or `sessionID`): every session started from it, directly or through others. |
| `courier_stop` | `sessionID`, `cleanup?` | [Stops](#seeing-and-stopping-a-subtree) a session below this one and everything under it. |
| `courier_cleanup` | `sessionID`, `force?` | Forgets a child this session started itself, first removing its [worktree](#worktrees) if it is isolated. |
| `courier_answer` | `sessionID`, `requestID`, `reply?`, `message?`, `answers?` | Proposes `once` or `reject` for a [permission request](#a-child-that-asks-for-permission), or passes on your answers to a [question](#a-child-that-asks-a-question). |
| `courier_later` | `message`, `sessionID?`, `delayMinutes?` or `at?` | Schedules a [message](#scheduled-messages) for a session (this one by default), in `delayMinutes` or at an ISO 8601 time. Returns its id. |
| `courier_cancel` | `id` | Drops a scheduled message. |

## The model a child runs on

A child runs on the first model named of: `courier_spawn`'s `model` (`provider/model`, as OpenCode
names them: `opencode/gpt-5-nano`), its `agent`'s model, its parent's model. `variant`, OpenCode's
name for a model's reasoning effort (`low`, `medium`, `high` or whatever the model has; `default` is
the provider's own), replaces the chosen model's variant. A `model` without a `variant` runs at that
model's default, not at the parent's variant. A parent whose session names no model runs on
OpenCode's default; its children are started on it and stay on it if the default changes.

A model OpenCode does not list, or a variant the model lacks, is refused with what is listed, and
nothing starts. When the listing cannot be read, the choice goes through unchecked, and a wrong one
fails the child's first turn, which is [reported](#a-child-that-fails). A child on another model than
its parent's is named with it, as `provider/model#variant`, in the spawn's result, in `courier_tree`
and in the [tree panel](#the-tree-panel).

## Session trees and their limits

Any spawned session can call `courier_spawn` too, so sessions form a tree. The session nobody
spawned is its top, at depth 0. `courier_spawn` refuses a spawn, naming the limit and what to do
instead, when the child would be deeper than `maxDepth`, or when `maxChildren` or `maxTotal`
sessions are already live. Several spawns made at once cannot get past a limit together.

A session is live while:

- its turn runs, unless it has already sent its parent a report other than `blocked` in that turn,
  so a parent woken by a report can start the next part in the same turn;
- it [owes its parent a report](#a-child-that-ends-without-a-report);
- its last report is `blocked`, as it waits on its parent's answer; this makes no session above it
  live, since no report of its own will wake them;
- a message sent to wake it waits in its inbox, unless it is [stalled](#a-missed-wake);
- a session below it is live.

So a child that is `blocked`, or that ended its turn without reporting, counts until it reports or
its parent drops it with `courier_cleanup`, even after a stop; so does a session waiting for its own
children. Renaming, archiving or switching a session's model does not make it live.

**The brief.** Each spawned session gets its task with a brief: its depth, the limits, how to
report, and whether to split. Below `maxDepth` it splits a task with two or more independent,
substantial parts, one session per part, and does a smaller one itself; at `maxDepth` it does the
task itself. Its decision is one line in its transcript: `split: no, because …` or
`split: <n> parts: …`; the root may also write `split: 1 part: …` to hand a heavy task whole to one
session and keep its own context. A session that splits ends its turn while the parts work and
sends its parent one combined report. A finding the other parts need goes up at once, as a message
without a status. Text you type into a spawned session is passed up by courier
([steering](#steering-a-running-tree)), and its report says what it did because of it.

**The tools a leaf is offered.** A leaf cannot start sessions, so it is offered only `courier_send`,
`courier_tree`, `courier_later` and `courier_cancel`, as is a subagent [OpenCode's subagent
tool](#opencodes-subagents) starts in a tree. Every other session is offered all eight. If you lower
`maxDepth` while a session has children, it may become a leaf with children it cannot stop or clean
up itself: a session above it does that with `courier_stop` and `cleanup: true`, or you stop them in
the [tree panel](#the-tree-panel).

## The courier-orchestrate skill

The plugin registers one OpenCode skill, `courier-orchestrate`, in every location: how its tools
behave when a session splits a task. Models load it when they decide whether to split a task; a
spawned session is told to load it too, except a leaf. In the TUI, `/skills` attaches it to your
prompt. Without it, the brief, the tool descriptions and courier's notices still carry the rules.
Loading it asks the `skill` permission like any skill. To hide it, deny it in `permissions`:
`{ "action": "skill", "resource": "courier-orchestrate", "effect": "deny" }`.

Each check a part runs and each skill it loads may ask a permission, and every request below the
top waits on you: a permission rule that allows the project's check scripts (run through them, not
a tool's own path) and one for `skill` keep the tree from stalling on them.

How to shape the work (which parts a task has, when to stage a tightly coupled core, how a review
after the merge runs, which checks to run) is not in the plugin: write it as a skill of your own.
`courier-orchestrate` tells a model to load such a skill when one is listed, and a parent names the
skills each part should load. OpenCode reads your skills from `~/.config/opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`,
and from a project's `.opencode/skills/`, `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/`; in a project the
skill must be committed, since an isolated child's worktree starts from `HEAD`.

## A child's report

A child reports with `courier_send` to its parent, with a `status`:

- `done`;
- `partial`: some of the task is left, and the report says what and why;
- `blocked`: it needs a decision from its parent, and says what;
- `failed`.

Any other status is refused. A report may list `artifacts`: `branch` (a string), `commits` and
`files` (lists of strings), and `checks` (a list of `{ command, result }`). A message with a status
settles the child's report, `blocked` included. A message without one is progress and settles
nothing.

## A child that fails

For every failed turn of a spawned session (no model, missing credentials, the provider down), not
stopped with `courier_stop`, the parent gets a message from that child with the error, which wakes
it if idle. The parent can message the child to try again, start a replacement, or carry on. While
sessions under the child are still [live](#session-trees-and-their-limits), their reports will wake
it, so no replacement is offered.

When the provider says how long a rate or quota limit lasts, the message says until when, and the
tree panel shows the row as `limit, resumes 14:32`. Courier does not retry for you; a
[check-in](#check-ins) can remind the parent.

An interrupted turn is not a failure. A failure while the server is down is not seen, which is what
a [check-in](#check-ins) is for.

## A child that ends without a report

A spawned session owes its parent a report from the moment a task or message reaches it until it
reports with a status, or its turn fails or is interrupted. What you type in the child's own session
does not make it owe one, nor does a progress message from one of its own children or its own
check-in firing after it has reported.

Before it goes idle owing a report, the child is reminded once, in the same turn, and the parent is
not woken. If it still ends its turn without a report, the parent gets a message saying so, with the
start of the child's last reply, and can tell the child to carry on or report, or start a
replacement.

The parent is not told while the child waits on something: its own children's reports, a permission
request or question, a scheduled message, or background work of its own (a shell, a subagent). A
turn stopped by a server shutdown resumes on the next start and is not told. A turn ended by a plain
permission decline or a dismissed question is told, without a reminder.

## A missed wake

OpenCode starts a turn when a message lands in an idle session's inbox. Rarely, it does not. So
courier watches every message it sends to wake a session, and sends one that is still waiting after
about half a minute once more. If the session still has not taken it, it is **stalled**: the footer
counts it and the tree panel marks its row. Prompting the session delivers the message and ends the
stall.

## A child that asks for permission

When a child's tool call needs approval, OpenCode holds it until someone answers in the child's
session. Courier tells the top session what the child asks for. A request from any depth goes to the
top, and only the top can answer it; a sub-orchestrator is not told of its children's requests or
questions.

The top session's model cannot approve. It proposes an answer with
`courier_answer { sessionID, requestID, reply, message? }`:

- `once`: OpenCode first checks the request against the top session's own rules. When they say ask,
  it shows you its permission prompt there. `once` reaches the child only if you allow it. A rule
  that denies it in the top session refuses it.
- `reject`: refuses it, with a reason if given.

In the prompt, *Allow once* passes it on. *Reject* with a reason refuses the child's request with
that reason. A plain *Reject* ends the top session's step and leaves the child's request waiting.

`always` is not offered through `courier_answer`, since it would save a rule for the parent's whole
project. Grant a standing rule where OpenCode shows the child's own request: in the child's session,
or the [asks inbox](#the-asks-inbox).

A rejection always carries a message, so the child's call fails and the child carries on.

A request answered elsewhere (in the child's session, the asks inbox, or by an `always` that covers
it) is settled: the top session gets a short note that waits for its next turn and wakes nothing. A
rejection in OpenCode rejects the other pending requests of the same step too; the note then says
the child may have stopped and `courier_send` restarts it. Requests still waiting are in
[`courier_tree`'s `pending`](#seeing-and-stopping-a-subtree).

## A child that shows a form

Some OpenCode forms can only be answered in the child's session. The common one is web search's
first call with no provider chosen. Courier tells the top session; answer it in the child's session
or the [asks inbox](#the-asks-inbox). Once the form is answered or cancelled, the top session gets a
note, which wakes it if idle.

OpenCode waits a minute for a web search choice, then the child's search fails and it carries on.
The choice is global: make it once, in any session, or under OpenCode's "Third-party search"
setting. Forms of sessions courier did not spawn, such as MCP servers' requests, are ignored.

## A child that asks a question

When a child calls OpenCode's `question` tool, courier sends the top session, from any depth, the
questions and their options. The top session should ask you the same questions with its own question
tool. When the wording and options match, the two are linked: your pick goes straight to the child,
which carries on in the same turn. Otherwise the top passes your answer with
`courier_answer { sessionID, requestID, answers }`: one entry per question, a label, your own text,
or a list of labels.

The question stays in the child's session too, and the first answer counts. Dismissing it in the
child's session ends the child's turn. Dismissing it in the top session ends the top's turn, and the
child carries on without an answer.

A question answered in the child's session or the asks inbox, without the top's own question,
sends the top a note, which wakes it if idle.

A question whose call is cut off (the child's turn stopped, a restart) stays answerable, and your
answer reaches the child as a message. Unanswered questions are kept for up to 14 days, at most the
100 newest, and while their session is in the [roster](#roster).

A child whose agent may not use the question tool (OpenCode's `general` agent, or a deny rule) can
still ask with `courier_send`.

## Seeing and stopping a subtree

**`courier_tree`** lists the sessions under a session, depth first, at most `maxTotal`: the live
ones first, then the newest, with a count of any left out. Each entry has the session's state, its
last reply, the permission requests and questions it waits on (`pending`; forms are not listed) and
whether it owes a report. [OpenCode's subagents](#opencodes-subagents) in the tree are listed too.
Anyone can read any tree.

**`courier_stop { sessionID, cleanup? }`** stops a session and every session under it:

1. Only a session above the target may stop it.
2. The `courier_later` messages scheduled for them are cancelled.
3. They are interrupted deepest first, [OpenCode's subagents](#opencodes-subagents) among them. Each
   says `interrupted`, `idle` (it was not running), `gone` (OpenCode does not have it) or `failed`
   (it may still run). An `idle` one that owed its report still owes it and counts toward the
   limits until its parent drops it with `courier_cleanup`.
4. With `cleanup: true`, their worktrees are removed by `courier_cleanup`'s rules, without `force`.

When the target was interrupted, or idle owing a report or after reporting `blocked`, its parent is
told once, unless it is the caller; sessions under the target are not told. A stopped session stays
in the tree and can be messaged again. A session started by the subtree while the stop runs may
escape it. A stop leaves background jobs running: one ending wakes the session, whose parent is
told it did not report.

## Steering a running tree

You steer a running tree by talking to any session in it. In the `/courier tree` panel
([In the terminal](#in-the-terminal)), `enter` opens any session, and what you type goes to it like
in any chat. A running session takes it into its current turn. Courier passes the text on to every
session above it, so the tree's top sees it too, and a parent with the skill passes it to the parts
it changes.

**What is passed.** Only the text, cut at 4000 characters: files, agents and skills attached to it
stay behind. Courier cannot tell who wrote a prompt, so it passes any prompt that arrives as text: what
you type in the TUI or send with `opencode run --session` or the API, a slash command's whole
template, the typed part of a prompt with a skill attached. The TUI's `!` shell commands, courier's
own messages and OpenCode's automations are not passed.

**When.** The text is passed only while the tree is at work: a session under the top is running or
`blocked`, the session you typed into owes a report or has a courier message waiting, or the top
session's turn is running. Once the top has ended its turn and every session has reported, text you
type into a session under it stays there.

The sessions above get it as progress, not a prompt, so they owe no report for it.

**Other ways to reach the tree.** `courier_send` without a `status` is an ordinary message, so a
parent can pass a finding on to its other children. A `status` on a message to a session below the
sender is dropped, and the result says so.

## Roster

`courier_spawn` records each child under its parent, so `courier_tree` finds them after a
compaction or restart. A child deleted in OpenCode is forgotten at once, unless it is isolated or
has children of its own. Other entries are dropped 14 days after the child started, except isolated
children whose worktree is still there.

**Forking a session in a tree.** A fork (OpenCode's `/fork`) copies a session's transcript, so a fork
of a child reads the child's brief, and a fork of a parent reads of children it never started. A
fork is a top session of its own: `courier_tree` lists nothing in it, and the original's children
keep reporting to the original. Courier tells the fork so before its first prompt. A fork of a leaf
can start sessions.

## Worktrees

An isolated child works in a git worktree under OpenCode's data directory, on a detached HEAD. It is
told to commit on a branch named `courier/<its session ID>` and to name it in `artifacts.branch`.
Its parent merges that branch.

The worktree starts from the project's last commit; an isolated child of an isolated child starts
from the commit its parent's worktree is on. Uncommitted work, project skills included, is never
handed down: `courier_spawn` warns when the parent's working tree has uncommitted changes, untracked
files included. In a directory that is no git repository there is no warning and the spawn goes on.
If an isolated parent's HEAD cannot be read, the spawn fails; start it without `isolate`.

Nothing removes a worktree on its own. When the parent has what it needs, it calls
`courier_cleanup { sessionID }`. The worktree is kept, and the result says why, when it holds
uncommitted changes (untracked files included, ignored ones not), or commits on no branch, tag or
remote, and the child is not dropped: `courier_tree` still lists it and it counts toward the limits.
Commit what you want to keep to a branch and call again, or call with `force: true` to discard it. A
child without `isolate` has no worktree: `courier_cleanup` only forgets it. `courier_cleanup` never
deletes a session. Call it after the child has reported.

## Scheduled messages

`courier_later` takes `delayMinutes` or `at`, an ISO 8601 time not in the past, and a `sessionID`
(by default the caller), which may be any session. A message arrives within about a second of its
time, waits behind a running turn and survives a restart; a crash at the wrong moment can deliver it
twice. With [two servers](#two-servers-on-one-data-directory), one scheduled less than 15 seconds
ahead on the server that does not deliver can be up to 15 seconds late. One that cannot be delivered
is logged and dropped. OpenCode loads plugins when a project is first used after a start, so
messages that fell due meanwhile arrive then.

A spawned session cannot use OpenCode's automations (`automation_create` and the rest): a wake-up of
theirs goes round the tree, so the child would read as having ended without a report.
`courier_later` is the way for a child to wait. Nor can it use OpenCode's session interrupt
(`opencode_session_interrupt`, with `experimental.full_codemode`), which would stop its parent or a
sibling without telling the tree: `courier_stop` is the way. A root session keeps both.

### Check-ins

A `courier_later` message a session schedules for itself is a check-in. A parent's check-in covers
what courier cannot see: a child's failure while the server was down, or the end of a rate limit's
wait. A spawned session that waits on something outside the tree, such as an OpenCode Console event
watch, is asked to tell its parent and schedule itself a check-in before it ends its turn, so it
reads as waiting, not as ended without a report. A report does not cancel a check-in: only
`courier_cancel` does, or [`courier_stop`](#seeing-and-stopping-a-subtree) of the session it is
for.

## `/goal` and courier children

OpenCode's `/goal` has a reviewer check the session each time its turn ends and
prompts it to continue unless the goal is met, blocked or paused. It holds back only for OpenCode's
own background work, not for courier children, and a plugin cannot change that; [an upstream
request](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/60860) asks OpenCode for a way to.

So a session with an active goal that ends its turn to wait for its children is prompted to continue
at once. It may poll, redo the children's work or spawn again, until the goal pauses (`Not making
progress`). The children carry on, and their reports wake the session as usual.

Don't set a goal on a session that waits on courier children: their reports wake it, and a
[check-in](#check-ins) covers the rest. A goal on a session that does the work itself is not affected.
Once the reports are in, `/goal resume` picks a paused goal up again.

## Native child sessions

A native child is an OpenCode subagent of its parent. The parent chooses per spawn with
`courier_spawn`'s `native`: `true` makes that child a subagent; unset or `false` keeps it a
standalone session. A tree may mix both kinds. Leave it unset for a part you may want to open or
that should outlive the parent. Use native children only with OpenCode's TUI or the paired app,
which show their prompts. What changes for a native child:

- **Asks are answered in OpenCode's view.** A native child's permission requests, questions and
  forms show in the TUI's view, and the paired app's request dock, of its nearest ancestor that is
  not itself a native child. The top session's model is only told of them. With a bare API client
  nothing shows the prompts: `courier_answer` is the fallback, with the ids from `courier_tree`'s
  `pending`.
- **OpenCode reports each turn's end too**, with a message of its own that wakes the parent. So each
  child turn costs an extra parent turn, at every native level above it. Native children are worth
  it for OpenCode's own view of the children, not for fewer turns.
- **Deleting a session deletes its native children.**
- **The child gets courier's own permission rules**, not its parent's session rules, as a standalone
  child does.
- **Providers see a subagent.** GitHub Copilot meters subagents differently; courier is not tested
  on Copilot.
- **A native child leaves the TUI's session lists.** Reach it from the parent's subagent tab.
- **`autoaccept` and `opencode run`** in the session whose view shows a native child's asks answer
  them: `autoaccept` and `run --auto` approve them, `run` without `--auto` rejects them. `opencode
  run` waits for native children, and may not exit when one ends after the run's own last turn.
- **`courier_tree` and the [tree panel](#the-tree-panel)** mark it `native`.

An isolated child cannot be native: `native: true` with `isolate: true` is refused. A tree with
isolated children shows in OpenCode as several trees, split at each isolated child; `courier_tree`
shows the whole.

## OpenCode's subagents

A session in a tree may start subagents with OpenCode's own `subagent` tool. Courier finds them
under every session of the tree, subagents' own subagents too.

- **`courier_tree` and the [tree panel](#the-tree-panel)** list them under the session that started
  them, marked `subagent`, with what they do and cost. They owe no report. `enter` opens one; `s`
  and `x` do not act on one, which is stopped with the session above it.
- **[`courier_stop`](#seeing-and-stopping-a-subtree)** interrupts them with the rest of the subtree,
  since they would otherwise outlive it. A subagent cannot be the target itself.
- **A leaf's tools.** A subagent is offered only the four tools a leaf is offered. A subagent of
  a session in no tree is a top session like any other.

They are not counted in the [status entry](#the-status-entry), where OpenCode's own footer counts
them, nor against the [limits](#session-trees-and-their-limits). Their asks show in OpenCode's TUI,
and are not relayed.

## In the terminal

The package ships a part for OpenCode's terminal UI, loaded from the server's plugin list. The
server part works the same without it.

### The status entry

In the prompt's footer, for the open session:

```
courier 1 waiting on you · 1 stalled · 2 running · 1 idle
```

It counts the sessions started with `courier_spawn` under the open one: waiting on you (a
permission request, question or form), stalled, running, then idle. While anything waits on you, a
click on it opens the [asks inbox](#the-asks-inbox). While a permission prompt or form shows,
OpenCode hides the footer; use `ctrl+x k`. Right after the server starts, the entry may take a few
seconds to show.

### The tree panel

`/courier tree` (or *Courier session tree* in the palette) opens a panel beside the session with
the session's whole tree, from its root, the open session marked `(on screen)`. It is fullscreen
under 108 columns.

```
 █▀██▀██  courier tree  [█████░░░░░] 1/2 reported
▄▀▀▀▀▀▀▀  1 waiting on you · 1 idle
▸   Fix the login bug (on screen)  idle
  │ ran 4m 10s · last courier_spawn 2m 05s ago · ctx 12% · $0.03
  ├ ✓ Report back to your parent.  idle · reported done
  │   ran 12s · last courier_send 3s ago · $0.00
  └ ● CHILD-ASKS  waiting on you · owes a report
      asks permission: shell echo courier-asks
↑↓ select · enter open · s stop · x forget · r refresh · f fullscreen · q close
```

Keys: `↑`/`k` and `↓`/`j` move, `enter` or a click opens the session, `s` stops it, `x` forgets a
`gone` one, `r` refreshes, `f` toggles fullscreen and `q` closes. `<leader>left` and
`<leader>right` move the keyboard between the session and the panel. The panel follows you from
session to session, showing each one's tree. It hides on a screen with no session, and in a
session with no tree unless you opened it there.

**Stopping.** `s` asks you to confirm, then stops the selected session as `courier_stop` would from
the tree's root: any session in the tree but the root itself, whichever session is open. Its parent
is told unless that parent is the root.

**Forgetting.** `x` on a `gone` row (deleted in OpenCode, kept for its worktree or its children)
forgets it as `courier_cleanup` would from its parent, never with `force`, after a confirm. Like
`s`, it reaches any row in the tree but the root. A live row is never forgotten.

**Sounds.** A standalone child's report plays OpenCode's `subagent_done` sound.

### The asks inbox

Every permission request, question and form waiting on you anywhere in the tree, answered with no
model in between. Open it with `ctrl+x k` (`<leader>k`), `/asks` (or `/ask`), the palette's
"Courier: what waits on you", or a click on the footer.

The top session's own requests come first, chiefly the prompts `courier_answer once` opens; allowing
one passes `once` on to the child. Choosing an ask opens its dialog, and `esc` goes back. A
permission request offers `Allow once`, `Always allow` (when it has a rule to save) and `Reject`,
with or without a reason. A form is asked field by field, a question one question at a time, with
your own answer where it allows one. A form that opens a page is answered in its own session.

New asks play OpenCode's own sounds. A native child's new ask, which OpenCode does not announce,
also shows a notification naming its path in the tree.

## Two servers on one data directory

Two OpenCode servers on one data directory, such as `opencode serve` next to `opencode service`,
share the plugin's storage but not its memory:

- Scheduled messages are delivered, and missed wakes sent again, by one server. If it stops, another
  takes over within about 75 seconds.
- A child's permission request, failure or silent end is told once, by the server running it.
  Whether a child owes a report compares both servers' clocks, so run them on one machine.
- `courier_answer` passes an answer on only from the server where the child waits, and
  `courier_tree` lists only that server's requests.

Where you can, run one server per data directory, or point a second one at another
(`XDG_DATA_HOME`).
